name: Morph filter: LFO-cycle one filter continuously through LP → BP → HP → notch → LP
goal: Animate pads, leads and repetitive noisy synths with a single continuous morph filter whose shape glides LP → bandpass → highpass → notch → back to LP, driven by a free-running (non-retriggered) LFO at 20–80% depth, optionally followed by a static classic low-pass, with LFO2 on cutoff and a little per-note random on the morph — a dedicated filter-shape morph recipe, distinct from parallel-filter chains, dual-path stereo spread and filter-flavor (ladder/diode/comb) choice.

source.title: Why does nobody use this filter ? (Ableton Morph Filter Tutorial)

prerequisites: Synth with a morphing (multi-mode continuous) filter, or 4 parallel filters (LP/BP/HP/notch) you can crossfade
Two LFOs and a mod matrix; a per-note random source

inputs.name: source_patch
inputs.description: Pad, lead or percussive noisy synth to animate

inputs.name: morph_lfo_rate
inputs.description: Slow for pads, faster/BPM-synced for rhythmic motion

outputs.name: morphing_patch
outputs.description: Patch whose filter shape continuously morphs

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.

Implementation note (not from transcript): in Web Audio emulate the morph with four parallel BiquadFilterNodes (lowpass/bandpass/highpass/notch) sharing one frequency/Q and crossfade adjacent pairs with equal-power gains driven by the morph position (0–4 wrapping).
Distinct from parallel-filter-rhythmic-pad-chains and dual-path-filter-spread-inverse-amp-lfo-stereo: one filter changes TYPE over time; cutoff motion is secondary.

steps.action: Select the morph filter mode. Understand the morph control: 0 = low-pass leaning toward the next shape; at 100 it is fully bandpass, then it continues to highpass, then notch, then back toward low-pass.
steps.expect: One knob sweeps through LP, BP, HP, notch in order

steps.action: Set the slope to 24 dB and add a bit of resonance so the shape changes are clearly visible/audible while sweeping morph by hand.
steps.expect: Audible character change at each stage of the morph

steps.action: In the mod matrix route LFO1 → filter morph at 100%, then pull the LFO amount back into the 20–80% range. Turn retrigger OFF so the motion continues across notes.
steps.expect: Continuous filter-shape movement not restarting on each key

steps.action: Pick the LFO rate: slow for pad movement, faster or tempo-synced for rhythmic motion. Then adjust the morph default position, cutoff frequency, LFO amount and rate together to find the sweet spot.
steps.expect: Smooth, musical shape motion rather than jumpy sweeps

steps.action: Use the second filter slot as a static classic low-pass after the morph filter to keep the tone in check while the morph adds movement.
steps.expect: Movement without large changes to overall tone/character

steps.action: Optionally add LFO2 → cutoff frequency (subtle), or replace filter 2 with a second morph filter whose morph is driven by LFO2 (try a different waveform).
For percussive/noisy or robotic repetitive sounds, apply the morph filter with a different LFO waveform and rate to smooth the sound.
steps.expect: Robotic repetition becomes smoother and more alive

steps.action: Add a small amount of per-note Random (MIDI/mod matrix) to the morph amount/position so each note lands on a slightly different filter shape; A/B with the filter bypassed.
steps.expect: Subtle note-to-note variation; bypass sounds static by comparison

verification: Sweeping morph by hand passes audibly through LP, BP, HP and notch.
With LFO1 at 20–80% and retrigger off, motion continues smoothly across held chords.
Bypass A/B: morph-filtered version has clearly more movement.
